solution_approaches.quote: Variational quantum simulation (VQS) can also be used to simulate the solution for certain PDEs as the evolution of a quantum state. key_claims.claim: Quantum Monte Carlo integration and gradient estimation can provide a quadratic speedup over classical methods but require significant resource reductions for practical advantage.
key_claims.quote: Quantum Monte Carlo integration and gradient estimation can provide quadratic speedup over classical methods, but more work is required to reduce the amount of quantum resources for early fault-tolerant feasibility and achieving an actual speedup.

key_claims.claim: Quantum algorithms for stochastic modeling, optimization, and machine learning are broadly applicable to financial problems.
key_claims.quote: Quantum algorithms for stochastic modeling, optimization, and machine learning are applicable to a variety of ﬁnancial problems.

key_claims.claim: Current quantum hardware is in a nascent NISQ stage with low fidelity and few qubits, severely limiting solvable problem sizes.
key_claims.quote: Moreover, current quantum hardware is still in a nascent stage, existing noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices (NISQ) have low ﬁdelity and a small number of qubits, which severely limits the size of problems that can be solved.

key_claims.claim: End-to-end quantum advantage in commercially relevant financial problems is challenged by data loading, readout, and pre/post-processing costs.
key_claims.quote: In particular, a large amount of work needs to be done to reduce the resource requirements in certain components of the algorithms, such as quantum embedding of classical input data, readout of the quantum output, and pre- and post-processing. Otherwise, the complexity of these components may signiﬁcantly disparage the speedup obtained from other components of the algorithm.

key_claims.claim: The overhead from current quantum error correcting codes could prevent the quadratic speedup of QMCI from being realizable in practice.
key_claims.quote: In addition, it has been noted that the overhead from current quantum error correcting codes could prevent the quadratic speedup from being realizable 28.
key_claims.location: Page 3, Quantum methods for Monte Carlo-based pricing and risk analysis, paragraph 2

key_claims.claim: State preparation for QMCI is a major bottleneck, especially for concentrated distributions and tabulated data.
key_claims.quote:
Despite the general applicability of these algorithms, their inverse dependence on the ﬁlling ratio (the relevant norm of the function divided by the corresponding norm of the bounding box of that function) of the function being loaded, makes these algorithms much less efﬁcient when the target distribution is concentrated around a few values.
...
For loading tabulated data, one has to resort to generic data loading techniques 47–49, which in general scale linearly with the number of data points to be loaded.

key_claims.claim: It remains an open question whether there are unitary procedures for loading payoff distributions that avoid heavy arithmetic and scale sublinearly in qubits.
key_claims.quote: Therefore, it remains an open question whether there are alternative unitary procedures for loading the payoff distribution that avoid signiﬁcant arithmetic and have sublinear scaling in the number of qubits.
key_claims.location: Page 4, Quantum methods for Monte Carlo-based pricing and risk analysis, paragraph on joint distribution loading

key_claims.claim: For PDE-based pricing, quantum linear systems algorithms can offer exponential reduction in dimension dependence but suffer from sampling overhead similar to QMCI.
key_claims.quote: Whereas under various assumptions about the conditioning of the linear systems and data-access model, the quantum linear system can be solved with an exponential reduction in the dependence on the dimension, a sampling cost needs to be paid to readout the solution from the quantum state, making this technique reminiscent of classical and quantum MCI.
key_claims.location: Page 5, Quantum methods for differential-equation-based pricing and risk analysis, paragraph 2

key_claims.claim: For structured convex programs like SCPs, there is currently only a small margin for practical quantum speedup because classical methods are already very efficient.
key_claims.quote: Considering that SCPs can be solved very efﬁciently classically, there is a small margin for quantum speedup in practice.
key_claims.location: Page 6, Quantum methods for continuous optimization, paragraph 4

key_claims.claim: Quantum BLAS-based speedups are challenged by conditioning dependence, sampling costs, and data loading requirements.
key_claims.quote: However, a quantum BLAS (QBLAS) 59, 87 comes with three notable caveats that make it challenging to compare quantum and classical worst-case complexities. First, a QBLAS operates on the spectrum of matrices and thus has polynomial dependence on the conditioning of the matrix, which classically typically appears only in iterative algorithms. Second, retrieving data from a quantum device requires sampling and consequently incurs a classical sampling cost that depends poorly on the desired error. Lastly, the algorithms require access to the classical data in quantum superposition, which can only be done efﬁciently without quantum memory in certain cases when the input matrices are sparse.
key_claims.location: Page 6–7, Quantum methods for continuous optimization, paragraph on QBLAS caveats

key_claims.claim: It is still an open question whether quantum computation can provide an advantage for structured convex programs in general, including finance.
key_claims.quote: Currently, it seems to still be an open question whether quantum computation can provide an advantage for structured convex programs in general, and not just ﬁnance.
key_claims.location: Page 7–8, Quantum methods for continuous optimization, paragraph on overall assessment

key_claims.claim: Quantum walk search can provide almost quadratic speedup for tree search, but integration of practical heuristics and overall time-to-solution advantages remain unclear.
key_claims.quote: Ref. 120 developed quantum-walk-search-based techniques, which provide an almost quadratic speedup for tree search in terms of the size of the tree. However, this does not allow the integration of search heuristics or early stopping, both of which have been found to signiﬁcantly boost the performance of classical algorithms on typical problem instances.

key_claims.claim: For quantum simulated annealing, it is unclear whether all parameter dependencies can be improved over classical MCMC, and classical SA is usually used heuristically.
key_claims.quote: However, it’s still unclear whether, in general, the dependence on all parameters with quantum can be made better than or even match the dependence they have with classical MCMC 128. Furthermore, classical SA is typically used as a heuristic and not run until the Markov chains have converged to their stationary distributions129, 130.

key_claims.claim: Variational quantum algorithms face challenges such as NP-hard parameter tuning and barren plateaus, though convergence can occur in over-parameterized regimes.
key_claims.quote: Variational quantum algorithms usually suffer from difﬁculties in tuning the variational parameters and hyperparameters, which by itself can be NP-hard157. In addition, for certain initializations, the gradients with respect to the parameters can vanish even when the model is far from convergence158, 159, requiring exponentially-many samples to estimate them. Still, the convergence of VQE has been demonstrated in the over-parameterized regime 160, even with exponentially-small gradients.

key_claims.claim: Quantum ML algorithms that accelerate classical techniques typically require error-corrected quantum computers and quantum memory, whose feasibility is unclear.
key_claims.quote:
Quantum algorithms for ML can be further divided into method s for accelerating classical techniques, typically by
applying QBLASs, and quantum-native algorithms, which att empt to harness the classical intractability of quantum
simulation to build more expressive models. The former typi cally requires an error-corrected quantum computer,
whereas, it is argued that, the later may not and is more near t erm42. ... The most notable
one being data loading, and unfortunately, most of these alg orithms work in a setting with quantum memory 179, 180.
It is currently unclear if such a device can be constructed.

key_claims.claim: Many QBLAS-based quantum ML algorithms only yield speedups for low-rank data and not exponential speedups as once thought.
key_claims.quote:
F urthermore, a variety of these approaches only provide
speedups when the data has low-rank approximations, and in t his setting, the speedup is not exponential as it was once
thought.

key_claims.claim: It is unclear whether quantum-native models provide advantage on classical (non-quantum-generated) problems.
key_claims.quote:
Quantum-native models, such as quantum neural networks, qu antum circuit Born machine and quantum kernel
methods, circumvent the issues of QBLASs and can be intracta ble to classically simulate, however, it is currently
unclear if they provide advantage on classical problems.

key_claims.claim: Initial numerical evidence suggests the expressivity advantage of quantum-native models does not extend to classical problems.
key_claims.quote:
Sp eciﬁcally, although these methods can be more expressive,
this has only been shown to provide advantage for problems in volving data generated from quantum processes 182.
In addition, initial numerical evidence suggests this does not extend to classical problems 183.

key_claims.claim: Parameterized quantum methods like QNNs are challenging to train and lack efficient backpropagation comparable to classical NNs.
key_claims.quote:
Parameterized quan-
tum methods, such as QNNs, can be challenging to train in gene ral158 and do not currently have back-propagation
algorithms that are as efﬁcient as those for classical NNs.

key_claims.claim: Further research is needed to determine if exponential speedup of classical ML problems is still possible with quantum computing.
key_claims.quote:
However, there remain some quantum ML algorithms t hat do not rely on this low-rank assumption and may
remain impervious to dequantization 181. Further research is needed to determine if an exponential s peedup of classical
ML problems is still possible with quantum computing.

key_claims.claim: Quantum circuit learning with low-depth circuits implies important application opportunities in quantum algorithms for finance.
key_claims.quote:
This technique
is dubbed as quantum circuit learning 192, and has been numerically shown to allow for a low-depth circ uit, hence
implying important application opportunities in quantum a lgorithms for ﬁnance.

key_claims.claim: Quantum boosting algorithms reduce dependence on VC dimension but require access to quantum examples, which is a major limitation.
key_claims.quote:
Ref. 208 demonstrated a quantization of the
AdaBoost algorithm, which promises a quadratic reduction i n the dependence on the VC dimension. ... A major limitation for both approaches is that they need to h ave access to quantum examples,
which requires preparing quantum states encoding distribu tions over the training data.

key_claims.claim: Generative quantum ML leveraging sampling advantages is particularly promising for finance because many applications require sampling from complex distributions.
key_claims.quote:
One of the most promising
aspects of achieving potential quantum advantage lies in th e sampling advantage of quantum computers, especially
considering that many applications in ﬁnance require gener ating samples from complex distributions.
key_claims.location: Page 12 – Quantum methods for generative learning

key_claims.claim: QCBM at least matches and can surpass restricted Boltzmann machines as model size scales.
key_claims.quote:
Numerical simulations suggest that in the task o f learning the distribution, QCBM at least matches the
performance of the restricted Boltzmann machine and demons trates superior performance as the model scales 236.
key_claims.location: Page 12 – Quantum methods for generative learning

key_claims.claim: QGANs may exhibit exponential advantage over classical adversarial networks when data are measurements from high-dimensional spaces.
key_claims.quote:
The authors showed that when the da ta consists of samples of measurements made on high-
dimensional spaces, quantum adversarial networks may exhi bit an exponential advantage over classical adversarial
networks.
key_claims.location: Page 12 – Quantum methods for generative learning

key_claims.claim: Quantum-inspired dequantized algorithms refute many originally claimed exponential quantum speedups for ML but may still inspire useful algorithms for high-dimensional financial problems.
key_claims.quote:
Despite these algorithms refuting much of the originally c laimed exponential quantum speedups for ML,
they could potentially inspire useful algorithms for high- dimensional ﬁnancial problems.

key_claims.claim: It is still unclear whether proposed quantum approaches for stochastic modeling, optimization and ML can yield end-to-end quantum advantage on practical financial problems.
key_claims.quote:
Promising provable quantum advantages
have been discovered in certain black-box settings, such as MCI. However, it is still unclear whether any of these pro-
posed approaches for stochastic modeling, optimization an d ML can be turned into an end-to-end quantum advantage
on practical problems.

key_claims.claim: The financial industry is well positioned to be an early adopter of quantum computing because computational time and accuracy directly impact profit and loss.
key_claims.quote:
In ﬁnance, computational time and ac curacy can often directly translate to the proﬁt and loss
of the business for which the problems are being solved, inso much that any actual wall-clock speedup and associated
model performance improvement that new forms of computing c ould bring can have a tremendous impact on the ﬁnan-
cial industry. ... As a result , the ﬁnancial industry is perfectly positioned to be an earl y
adopter and take full advantage of quantum computing in the ﬁ eld of computational ﬁnance.

key_claims.claim: State preparation, especially loading classical probability distributions, is a common bottleneck in quantum algorithms for stochastic modeling in finance.
key_claims.quote:
As mentione d earlier, state preparation, speciﬁcally the loading of
quantum states encoding classical probability distributi ons, is a common task required in quantum algorithms for
stochastic modeling.

key_claims.claim: Financial problems are typically highly constrained, so native multi-qubit and specialized two-qubit interactions could significantly reduce circuit complexity for QAOA and quantum ML.
key_claims.quote:
As mentioned in the Optimization section, ﬁnancial proble ms
are typically highly constrained. Moreover, having access to a variety of native entangling gates may also motivate the
design and implementation of more efﬁcient circuits for qua ntum ML182.

key_claims.claim: Existing quantum memory technologies have fundamental limitations that make scalable, low-cost quantum memory without active error correction highly challenging.
key_claims.quote:
However, it has been recently highlighted that existing qu antum memory technologies have
fundamental limitations that make the realization of low-c ost and scalable quantum memory without active error cor-
rection highly challenging 290.

key_claims.claim: Current quantum hardware has much slower operation clock rates than classical computers, limiting practical usability of many quantum algorithms, especially variational ML.
key_claims.quote:
Additionally, the operation clock rate of the current quant um hardware is much slower compared to classical
computers; this is also a limiting factor in the practical us ability of many quantum algorithms. For example, quantum
variational algorithms for ML require a large number of high -quality circuit evaluations to estimate gradients throug h
sampling.

key_claims.claim: Current quantum error correction introduces significant overhead that may negate certain quantum speedups for finance.
key_claims.quote:
Moreover, current quantum error correction techniques
introduce a signiﬁcant additional overhead that potential ly negates certain quantum speedups for ﬁnance 28.

key_claims.claim: There remain many quantum-algorithmic challenges to achieve real-world quantum advantage in finance, but advancing hardware will enable benchmarking of more complex algorithms.
key_claims.quote:
We hope that this Review has highlighted that in addition to challenges in hardware technologies there are still a lot
of interesting quantum-algorithmic challenges to overcom e to bring about a real-world quantum advantage. As quan-
tum hardware advances, we expect to be able to benchmark more complex quantum algorithms, especially heuristic
ones, on interesting problems.

open_questions.question: How can quantum resource requirements for data embedding, readout, and pre/post-processing be reduced to enable end-to-end quantum advantage in finance?
open_questions.quote: In particular, a large amount of work needs to be done to reduce the resource requirements in certain components of the algorithms, such as quantum embedding of classical input data, readout of the quantum output, and pre- and post-processing.

problems by using quantum-native methods appears to be unli kely, there is still signiﬁcant algorithmic research that
needs to be done to be certain.
